There are lots and lots of different Chinese companies which are selling icemakers on Amazon which are very similar or the same as this one. There are a couple of differences between this one and many of the others. One is the fact that this one makes ten bullets of ice instead of nine… The other is the fact that this one has a timer so that it will not continue to run at times when you do not need it to, like when you’re sleeping.

The listing shows that this particular icemaker can make up to 33 pounds of ice in a twenty-four hour period. This might be true, but that is only if you continually remove the ice from the basket as it is being made. The ice maker makes the ten bullets of ice… Then place them into a basket. If you do not remove the ice from the basket, then it simply melts and refreeze is. Once the ice is in the basket, the machine will not keep the ice frozen. If you need a lot of ice, then you will need to manually remove the ice from the basket and place it into your own freezer.

This icemaker is made in China and being sold by Chinese coming on Amazon. It works quite well as long as you have the right expectations.

This is surprising for a relatively expensive cooktop from a reputable company, but there is a fix: The manual (available from the kitchenaid website) explains how to reduce the low setting. You take each knob off while the burner is on and turn a screw. You need a thin long screwdriver - I had to make one from a heavy wire hanger, filing the end to form the screwdriver blade, easier than it sounds. The low setting is now acceptable, but not quite as low as I'd like, though I have not tried to readjust it.

2. Standard 20" double burner griddles don't fit easily. We have to set ours diagonally. I've just found Lodges new 16" long griddles which should fit nicely[[ASIN:B002CMLTXG Lodge Double Play Reversible Grill Griddle]]. I've ordered one, so we'll see.

3. Markings are easily scratched. The markings on the stainless steel next to the knobs are slowly being scratched off, possibly by aggressive cleaning.

4. The burner tops are easily bumped from the correct alignment when cleaning. This affects the flame shape, and may be unsafe.

I'd buy this again if given the cooktop choices we had back in 2008.
